newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens may sell 900 mln DM dental unit.
newsitem.headline: Siemens may sell 900 mln DM dental unit.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said on Monday it may sell a dental technology unit that generates about 900 million marks ($528.7 million) in annual sales.
Siemens may also fold the unit into a joint venture, if it finds a partner, the company said in response to a reporter inquiry.
The dental technology unit employed about 2,750 workers worldwide and is part of Siemens medical technology activities, the spokesman said.
Medical technologies was expected to produce a loss in 1996/97, Siemens said last November. The business year ends September 30.
For 1995/96, medical technology reported sales of 7.1 billion marks and pre-tax profit of 30 million marks.

Earlier this year chief executive Heinrich von Pierer said Siemens planned to divest businesses with combined volume of about 3.5 billion marks this year. Each of the company's 250 business areas had to be able to sustain profitability and competitive strength in the global market, he said.
The firm hoped divestments would improve profitability, which was expected to remain level this year.
